A World After the Collapse

The world of Bad Eden is not simply a place where history unfolded.

It is a world that broke.

Long ago, reality was part of a vast cosmic structure known as Adam Kadmon—a living architecture that held imagination, matter, and meaning together in harmony.

Then that structure collapsed.

When it did, the world shattered into fragments.
Regions of reality separated from one another, forming the hex-shaped territories that now make up the map of the campaign.

These fragments still exist, still hold people and places and stories—but they no longer fit together the way they once did.

The world continues, but it is unfinished.

Living in the Fragments

Life did not disappear when the collapse occurred.

Communities survived.

Cultures adapted.

New societies formed within the fragments of reality that remained.

But the world carries the scars of what happened.

Across the hexes you may find:

• abandoned infrastructure from a previous age
• strange magical phenomena
• corrupted landscapes
• isolated settlements trying to rebuild
• powerful forces struggling to shape the future

The world is still alive—but it is unstable, mysterious, and full of unfinished stories.

A World Waiting to Be Repaired

The collapse did more than fracture geography.

It disrupted the deeper systems that once held reality together.

Connections between places weakened.
Balance between forces broke down.
Strange phenomena began appearing where the structure of the world had torn.

Yet within this broken landscape lies possibility.

The fragments of reality can still be explored.
Communities can still be rebuilt.
Connections between regions can still be restored.

The world may be damaged, but it is not beyond repair.

The Great Work

Many believe the fragments of reality can be restored.

The effort to repair the world is known as The Great Work.

No single group can accomplish this alone.

Instead, countless individuals and factions across the world struggle to stabilize regions, restore infrastructure, and push back against the forces that threaten what remains.

The actions of your faction are part of this larger effort.

Every hex you stabilize, every community you help, and every threat you confront contributes to the gradual restoration of the world.

A World of Discovery

Because so much was lost during the collapse, the world is filled with unknowns.

Explorers and factions constantly uncover:

• forgotten technologies
• ancient structures
• hidden knowledge
• strange creatures
• fragments of the world that existed before the collapse

Exploration is not only about survival.

It is about understanding what the world once was—and what it might become again.

Your Place in the World

The story of Bad Eden is not only about the collapse.

It is about what comes after.

Players take the roles of characters and factions working within this fractured reality.

Through exploration, difficult decisions, and acts of courage, you help shape the direction the world will take.

Will the fragments reconnect and grow stronger?

Or will instability and corruption spread further across the hexes?

The future of the world is still unwritten.

And your actions help decide what comes next.

In Simple Terms

The world of Bad Eden is a shattered reality full of mystery and possibility.

The past explains how the world broke.

The present challenges you to survive within it.

And the future depends on what you choose to build from the fragments that remain.
